questions.stem: A taxi fare is C = 3.60 + 2.10d dollars for a trip of d kilometres. What does 2.10 represent?
options: The total cost of a 1 km trip
The number of kilometres per dollar
The flag fall charged at the start
questions.explanation: The slope is the rate of change of cost with distance: each extra kilometre adds $2.10. The flag fall is the constant term, 3.60, the cost when d = 0.

questions.stem: A water bill is B = 25 + 3.2w dollars, where w is the number of kilolitres used. What does the B-intercept, 25, represent?
options: The cost of each kilolitre of water
The amount of water used when the bill is zero
The maximum bill a household can receive
The fixed charge paid even if no water is used
questions.explanation: The intercept is the value of B when w = 0, so it is the fixed charge. The cost per kilolitre is the slope, 3.2.

questions.stem: A water bill is B = 25 + 3.2w dollars for w kilolitres. What is the bill for 40 kL?
questions.explanation: B = 25 + 3.2 × 40 = 25 + 128 = $153. Leaving out the fixed charge gives $128.

questions.stem: A linear relationship has y = 17 when x = 2 and y = 29 when x = 6. What is its rule?
questions.explanation: The slope is (29 − 17)/(6 − 2) = 3, and 17 = 3 × 2 + c gives c = 11. Check: 3 × 6 + 11 = 29. Using 17 as the intercept forgets that x = 2 there, not 0.

questions.stem: A prepaid phone has credit C = 30 − 0.5t dollars after t minutes of calls. What does the t-intercept represent?
options: The credit at the start is $60
After 30 minutes the credit runs out
After 60 minutes the credit runs out
questions.explanation: Set C = 0: 30 − 0.5t = 0 gives t = 60, the time when the credit is used up. The starting credit is the C-intercept, $30.

questions.stem: Find the distance between (−1, 2) and (5, 10), and the midpoint of the interval joining them.
questions.explanation: The distance is √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10, and the midpoint is ((−1 + 5)/2, (2 + 10)/2) = (2, 6). Adding 6 + 8 gives 14, and 100 forgets the square root.

questions.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations 2x + y = 11 and x − y = 1.
questions.explanation: Adding the equations eliminates y: 3x = 12, so x = 4 and then y = 11 − 8 = 3. Check in the second equation: 4 − 3 = 1. The pair x = 5, y = 1 satisfies only the first equation.

questions.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 2y = 12 and x + 4y = 14.
questions.explanation: Doubling the first gives 6x + 4y = 24; subtracting the second gives 5x = 10, so x = 2 and y = 3. The pair x = 4, y = 0 satisfies only the first equation.

questions.stem: Two straight lines have the same slope but different y-intercepts. How many points of intersection do they have?
questions.explanation: Lines with the same slope are parallel, and different intercepts mean they never meet, so the simultaneous equations have no solution. Lines with the same slope and intercept are coincident.

questions.stem: How many solutions do the simultaneous equations 2x + 4y = 6 and x + 2y = 3 have?
questions.explanation: The first equation is twice the second, so both describe the same line: every point on it is a solution. The lines are coincident, not just parallel.

questions.stem: Two straight roads follow the lines y = 2x − 3 and y = −x + 9 on a map grid. Where do they intersect?
questions.explanation: Set 2x − 3 = −x + 9, so 3x = 12 and x = 4; then y = 2 × 4 − 3 = 5. The point (5, 4) swaps the coordinates.

questions.stem: Plan A costs $20 a month plus $0.10 a minute; plan B costs $35 a month plus $0.04 a minute. Which statement is correct?
options: They cost the same at 250 minutes; B is cheaper for more
They cost the same at 250 minutes; A is cheaper for more
They cost the same at 150 minutes; B is cheaper for more
B is always cheaper because its rate is lower
questions.explanation: 20 + 0.10m = 35 + 0.04m gives 0.06m = 15, so m = 250. Beyond that, B's lower rate makes it cheaper; below it, A's lower fixed charge wins.

questions.stem: For which value of k do the equations kx + 3y = 6 and 2x − y = 4 have no solution?
questions.explanation: The second line has slope 2, and the first has slope −k/3, so −k/3 = 2 gives k = −6. Then the lines are y = 2x + 2 and y = 2x − 4, parallel and distinct.

questions.stem: If y is inversely proportional to x, what happens to y when x is doubled?
questions.explanation: Inverse proportion means y = k/x, so replacing x with 2x gives k/(2x), half the original value. Doubling would be direct proportion.

questions.stem: Six workers take 20 days to finish a job. Assuming the time is inversely proportional to the number of workers, how long would 8 workers take?
questions.explanation: The product is constant: 6 × 20 = 120 worker-days, so 8 workers take 120/8 = 15 days. Using direct proportion gives 20 × 8/6 ≈ 26.7 days.

questions.stem: State the asymptotes of the hyperbola y = 1/x.
questions.explanation: y = 1/x is undefined at x = 0 and never equals 0, so the axes are its vertical and horizontal asymptotes. The lines y = x and y = −x are its axes of symmetry.

questions.stem: What are the asymptotes of the graph of y = 3/(x − 2)?
questions.explanation: The graph of y = 3/x is translated 2 units right, so the vertical asymptote is x = 2; the horizontal asymptote stays at y = 0. The 3 dilates the graph without moving the asymptotes.

questions.stem: Envelopes of a certain type all have area 216 cm². If the length is 18 cm, what is the width?
questions.explanation: For a fixed area, width = 216/length, an inverse proportion: 216/18 = 12 cm. Subtracting the length from the area gives 198, which treats the relationship as linear.

questions.stem: A graph of the form y = a/(x − c) has vertical asymptote x = −1 and passes through (1, 3). What is its rule?
questions.explanation: The asymptote x = −1 gives c = −1, so y = a/(x + 1). Substituting (1, 3): 3 = a/2, so a = 6. Writing x − 1 puts the asymptote at x = 1 instead.

questions.stem: In which quadrants does the graph of y = −4/x lie?
questions.explanation: When x > 0, y is negative (fourth quadrant), and when x < 0, y is positive (second quadrant). The graph of y = 4/x, without the minus sign, lies in the first and third.

questions.stem: What is the equation of the circle with centre (2, −3) and radius 5?
questions.explanation: A circle with centre (h, k) and radius r is (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r². The signs inside the brackets are opposite to the coordinates of the centre, and the right side is r², not r.

questions.stem: Find the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.
questions.explanation: Completing the square: (x − 3)² − 9 + (y + 2)² − 4 − 12 = 0, so (x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 25. The radius √12 forgets to add the 9 and the 4.

questions.stem: Find the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² + 8x − 2y + 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: (x + 4)² − 16 + (y − 1)² − 1 + 1 = 0 gives (x + 4)² + (y − 1)² = 16, so the radius is 4. The value 16 is the radius squared.

questions.stem: A mobile phone tower at (3, 4) on a grid in kilometres has a range of 10 km. Which location is outside its coverage?
questions.explanation: The distance from (3, 4) to (13, 9) is √(10² + 5²) = √125 ≈ 11.2 km, beyond the range. The others are √85 ≈ 9.2, 9 and √72 ≈ 8.5 km away.

questions.stem: A pizza shop at the origin delivers to every point within 5 km. Which describes the delivery region?
questions.explanation: Points within 5 km of the origin satisfy √(x² + y²) ≤ 5, that is x² + y² ≤ 25: the circle and its inside. The inequality ≥ 25 describes the points outside.

questions.stem: Which describes the graph of y² = x?
options: A parabola opening upwards; a function
A parabola opening to the right; a function
A hyperbola in the first and fourth quadrants
A parabola opening to the right; not a function
questions.explanation: For each x > 0 there are two y-values, √x and −√x, so the graph is a sideways parabola and fails the vertical line test. y = x² is the upward parabola.

questions.stem: What are the domain and range of y = √x?
options: Domain x ≥ 0, range all real y
Domain all real x, range y ≥ 0
questions.explanation: Square roots of negative numbers are not real, so x ≥ 0, and √x is never negative, so y ≥ 0. Both include 0 because √0 = 0.

questions.stem: How is the graph of y = −√x related to the graph of y² = x?
options: It is the lower half of y² = x
It is the upper half of y² = x
It is y² = x reflected in the y-axis
It is the whole of y² = x
questions.explanation: y² = x gives y = ±√x. Taking only the negative values gives the half below the x-axis, which is a function.

questions.stem: What must be true of a relation for it to be called a function?
options: each y-value comes from exactly one x-value
its graph is a straight line
its domain and range are the same
each x-value in the domain gives exactly one y-value
questions.explanation: A function assigns exactly one output to each input. Different x-values may share a y-value, as in y = x², which is still a function.

questions.stem: A student applies the vertical line test to a graph. Which result shows that the graph is a function?
options: The graph meets the y-axis exactly once
No vertical line meets the graph more than once
Every vertical line meets the graph exactly twice
No horizontal line meets the graph more than once
questions.explanation: If some vertical line cuts the graph twice, one x-value has two y-values, so the relation is not a function. The horizontal line test checks something else.

questions.stem: If f(x) = x² − 3x, find f(−2).
If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x², find f(g(3)).
questions.explanation: g(3) = 9, then f(9) = 2 × 9 + 1 = 19. Applying f first gives g(f(3)) = g(7) = 49, the other order.

questions.stem: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x + 4)?
questions.explanation: The expression under the square root must not be negative: x + 4 ≥ 0, so x ≥ −4. The value x = −4 is allowed because √0 = 0.

questions.stem: What is the range of f(x) = x² + 1, where x is any real number?
questions.explanation: x² is never negative, so x² + 1 is at least 1, and it equals 1 at x = 0. Every value above 1 is also reached.

questions.stem: The height of a plant is modelled by h = f(t), where t is the time in weeks. Which is the independent variable?
questions.explanation: In y = f(x) the input x is the independent variable and the output y depends on it. Here the height depends on time, so t is independent and goes on the horizontal axis.

questions.stem: Which set of ordered pairs is a function?
questions.explanation: Each first coordinate appears only once in the first set, so each input has one output; sharing the output 2 is allowed. The others repeat an x-value with different y-values.

questions.stem: What is the range of f(x) = 1/x for x ≥ 2?
questions.explanation: f(2) = 1/2, and as x increases 1/x decreases towards 0 without reaching it. So the range is 0 < y ≤ 1/2; 0 itself is excluded.

questions.stem: If f(x) = x², simplify f(a + h) − f(a).
questions.explanation: f(a + h) − f(a) = a² + 2ah + h² − a² = 2ah + h². Writing (a + h)² as a² + h² misses the middle term, and 2a + h is this result divided by h.
